When Bihar joined (1717 prose versus the 1733 table entry) and the Orissa cession date (January 1747 footnote versus 1751-52) are in conflict on the Nawabs page
Extent of the misls 1748-1761 and the detail of the 1762-1798 city-patch shape; the origin of Cliopatria's 1803-1806 remnant; who held Lahore before 1765 and Kasur before 1761

problems: Cliopatria's british-empire shape of 1762 holds the Bengal of the Nawabs (the Nawabs' dossier ends in June 1757 at Plassey; the 1757-1761 shape is a British client) and its 1803 shape holds all of Awadh (116,334 km2) although the Nawab kept about half until 1856: the british-empire (sa-06) and colour agents must draw both as British clients, not British territory, until 1765/1772 (Bengal) and 1856 (Awadh).

nawabs-of-bengal has a war (Battle of Buxar, 1764-65) outside its life span, kept because Cliopatria's shape runs to 1761; hyderabad-state has an occupation_start (Berar, 1853) with no occupation_end because no page opened dates the end of British administration; nawab-of-awadh counterpart 'benares-state' has no dossier yet. These are the only validator warnings.

Cliopatria's Hyderabad shapes 1727-1798 leave out the Aurangabad country (the Nizam's capital 1724-1763), which Cliopatria draws in its Mughal (1727), Maratha (1794-1804) and British (1805) rows; the maratha-empire and mughal-empire dossiers should be checked for the overlap.

Hyderabad's Ceded Districts are drawn in the Nizam's Cliopatria shape from 1727 while the Treaty of Seringapatam and Ceded Districts pages give them to Mysore until 1792; the kingdom-of-mysore dossier writer should check Mysore's holding of Bellary, Cuddapah and Kurnool before 1792.

The Sikh Confederacy dossier ends in 1799; Cliopatria's 1800-1806 remnant shapes are treated as separate misls and need bhangi-misl or another owner, otherwise they vanish from the map. sikh-empire (sa-05-f) records gains from sikh-confederacy in 1800 and 1802 that fall one to three years after this dossier's end.
